qe: If in a code language, BAT is written as 23 and CAT is written as 24, then how BALL will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में BAT को 23 और CAT को 24 लिखा जाता है, तो उसी कूट भाषा में BALL को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Direct Positional Sum Shortcut):
Step 1: 'BAT' aur 'CAT' ke letters ki alphabetical positions ka sum check karein:
- B(2) + A(1) + T(20) = 23
- C(3) + A(1) + T(20) = 24
Logic: Word me maujood sabhi aksharon ke standard place values ko direct joda gaya hai.
Step 2: 'BALL' ke letters ka sum karein:
- B = 2
- A = 1
- L = 12
- L = 12
$$\text{Total Sum} = 2 + 1 + 12 + 12 = 27$$
Correct '28'7 hai.

Method 2 (Step-by-Step Addition Method):
$$\text{B} (2) + \text{A} (1) + \text{L} (12) + \text{L} (12) = 3 + 24 = 27$$
Sahi uttar '27' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If in a certain code language A = 2, M = 26 and Z = 52, then how BET will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में A = 2, M = 26 और Z = 52 है, तो उसी कूट भाषा में BET को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Positional Value Doubling Shortcut):
Step 1: Har letter ki alphabetical position ko 2 se multiply kiya gaya hai:
- A(1) × 2 = 2
- M(13) × 2 = 26
- Z(26) × 2 = 52
Step 2: 'BET' ke letters ka basic sum nikal kar double karein:
- B = 2, E = 5, T = 20
$$\text{Sum} = 2 + 5 + 20 = 27$$
$$\text{Code} = 27 $\times$ 2 = 54$$
Correct option  54 hai.

Method 2 (Individual Doubling Method):
$$\text{BET} = (2 $\times$ 2) + (5 $\times$ 2) + (20 $\times$ 2) = 4 + 10 + 40 = 54$$
Sahi uttar '54' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: In a certain code language DEEP = 120 and RABIT = 250, then how HAIR will be written in the same language?
qh: किसी कूट भाषा में DEEP = 120 और RABIT = 250 है, तो उसी कूट भाषा में HAIR को क्या लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Sum × Number of Letters Shortcut):
Step 1: Rule check karein: $\text{Code} = (\sum \text{Positions}) \times \text{Number of Letters}$.
- 'DEEP': $(4 + 5 + 5 + 16) = 30$, aur letters $= 4 \implies 30 \times 4 = 120$.
- 'RABIT': $(18 + 1 + 2 + 9 + 20) = 50$, aur letters $= 5 \implies 50 \times 5 = 250$.
Step 2: 'HAIR' par apply karein:
- Positions ka sum: $H(8) + A(1) + I(9) + R(18) = 36$
- Number of letters $= 4$
$$\text{Code} = 36 $\times$ 4 = 144$$
Correct '120'44 hai.

Method 2 (Unit Digit Method):
Sum ka unit digit 6 hai ($8+1+9+8 = 26 \to 6$) aur 4 letters hain: $6 \times 4 = 24$ (unit digit 4 aayega). Vikalpon me sirf 144 ka unit digit 4 hai.
Sahi uttar '144' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If E = 5, HOTEL = 12, then how LAMB will be written in the code language?
qh: यदि E = 5, HOTEL = 12 है, तो कूट भाषा में LAMB को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Average of Letter Positions Shortcut):
Step 1: Rule: $\text{Code} = \frac{\sum \text{Positions}}{\text{Number of Letters}}$ (Letters ka average nikala gaya hai):
- E: $\frac{5}{1} = 5$
- HOTEL: $\text{Sum} = 8 + 15 + 20 + 5 + 12 = 60$, letters $= 5 \implies \frac{60}{5} = 12$.
Step 2: 'LAMB' par apply karein:
- Sum: $L(12) + A(1) + M(13) + B(2) = 28$
- Letters ki sankhya $= 4$
$$\text{Code} = $\frac{28}{4}$ = 7$$
Correct option  7 hai.

Method 2 (Direct Division Method):
$$12 + 1 + 13 + 2 = 28 \implies 28 / 4 = 7$$
Sahi uttar '7' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If KITES = 2, MONDAY = 2 and AIR = 2, then how SUNDAY will be written in the code language?
qh: यदि KITES = 2, MONDAY = 2 और AIR = 2 है, तो कूट भाषा में SUNDAY को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Vowel Count Shortcut Method):
Step 1: Diye gaye shabdon me vowels (A, E, I, O, U) count karein:
- KITES me vowels: I, E (Total = 2)
- MONDAY me vowels: O, A (Total = 2)
- AIR me vowels: A, I (Total = 2)
Logic: Code shabd me maujood kul swaron (vowels) ki sankhya hai.
Step 2: 'SUNDAY' me vowels dekhein:
- U aur A (kul 2 vowels hain)
$$\text{Code} = 2$$
Correct '1' hai.

Method 2 (Direct Observation):
Sabhi shabdon ka code unme aane wale vowels ki sankhya par aadharit hai, SUNDAY me 2 vowels hain, isliye code 2 hoga.
Sahi uttar '2' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If TO = 19, MY = 16, then how HE will be written in the code language?
qh: यदि TO = 19, MY = 16 है, तो कूट भाषा में HE को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Opposite Position Sum Shortcut):
Step 1: Reverse positions (27 - Position) ka sum nikalte hain:
- 'TO': T ka opposite G(7), O ka opposite L(12) → $7 + 12 = 19$.
- 'MY': M ka opposite N(14), Y ka opposite B(2) → $14 + 2 = 16$.
Logic: Har letter ke reverse alphabetical value ka sum liya gaya hai.
Step 2: 'HE' par same rule lagayein:
- H ka opposite letter S(19)
- E ka opposite letter V(22)
$$\text{Total Sum} = 19 + 22 = 41$$
Correct '39'1 hai.

Method 2 (Formula Method):
$$\text{Code} = (27 $\times$ 2) - (\text{H} + \text{E}) = 54 - (8 + 5) = 54 - 13 = 41$$
Sahi uttar '41' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If ZIP = 198, ZAP = 246, then how MAP will be written in the code language?
qh: यदि ZIP = 198, ZAP = 246 है, तो कूट भाषा में MAP को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Opposite Position Sum × 6 + 18 Shortcut):
Step 1: Letters ke reverse alphabetical values (opposite positions) ka sum nikalein:
- 'ZIP': Z ↔ A(1), I ↔ R(18), P ↔ K(11)
  $$\text{Sum} = 1 + 18 + 11 = 30$$
  $$\text{Code} = (30 $\times$ 6) + 18 = 180 + 18 = 198$$
- 'ZAP': Z ↔ A(1), A ↔ Z(26), P ↔ K(11)
  $$\text{Sum} = 1 + 26 + 11 = 38$$
  $$\text{Code} = (38 $\times$ 6) + 18 = 228 + 18 = 246$$
Logic: $\text{Code} = (\sum \text{Opposite Values}) \times 6 + 18$.
Step 2: 'MAP' par same formula apply karein:
- M ↔ N(14), A ↔ Z(26), P ↔ K(11)
  $$\text{Sum} = 14 + 26 + 11 = 51$$
  $$\text{Code} = (51 $\times$ 6) + 18 = 306 + 18 = 324$$
Correct '234'24 hai.

Method 2 (Factorized Shortcut Method):
Equation ko simplify karein: $(\text{Sum} \times 6) + 18 = (\text{Sum} + 3) \times 6$.
- 'MAP' ke opposite positions ka sum $= 51$.
$$\text{Code} = (51 + 3) $\times$ 6 = 54 $\times$ 6 = 324$$
Sahi uttar '324' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If DRIVER = 12, PEDESTRIAN = 20, then how ACCIDENT will be written in the code language?
qh: यदि DRIVER = 12, PEDESTRIAN = 20 है, तो कूट भाषा में ACCIDENT को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Letter Count Doubling Shortcut):
Step 1: Diye gaye shabdon me letters ki kul sankhya count karke use 2 se multiply kiya gaya hai:
- 'DRIVER' me 6 letters hain → $6 \times 2 = 12$
- 'PEDESTRIAN' me 10 letters hain → $10 \times 2 = 20$
Logic: $\text{Code} = \text{Number of letters} \times 2$.
Step 2: 'ACCIDENT' me letters count karein:
- A-C-C-I-D-E-N-T me kul 8 letters hain:
$$\text{Code} = 8 $\times$ 2 = 16$$
Correct '3'6 hai.

Method 2 (Direct Inspection Method):
Word ki length ka direct dugna answer hai: $8 \times 2 = 16$. options '3' and '8', (D) seedhe eliminate ho jate hain.
Sahi uttar '16' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.
